Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has publicly confirmed that preliminary talks are under way with SpaceX about building a commercial rocket launch site, but no site has been chosen, no contract signed and no timetable set.

Observers generally judge that the island development will most likely serve SpaceX’s core commercial line. The islands could host ground stations and telemetry‑control nodes for Starlink in the Asia‑Pacific, strengthening signal coverage over the South China Sea and the western Pacific; they would also take advantage of the Philippines’ low‑latitude position facing west to lower launch costs and provide backup landing spots for sea‑based rocket recovery and ship berthing.

The strategic coordinates are worth noting. The Philippines sits between the Bashi Channel and the Sulawesi Sea and is viewed by the United States as a core node of the “first island chain.” The US‑Philippines alliance, dating back to the 1947 Military Base Agreement and the 1951 Mutual Defense Treaty, has been reinforced by the 1998 Visiting Forces Agreement that allowed U.S. troops to return, and the 2014 Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement that solidified “shoulder‑to‑shoulder” joint exercises.

The Quad‑plus meeting of the United States, Japan, Australia and India was held in Manila last week, with the Philippines deeply embedded in the agenda, effectively becoming the on‑the‑ground vehicle for the Indo‑Pacific mechanism. If Musk places a piece on that board, his commercial empire would be almost perfectly aligned with Washington’s Indo‑Pacific strategy.

However, domestic politics in the United States is pushing back. Musk got his start with Democratic‑run California clean‑energy subsidies, but after 2020 shifted to the Republican camp when the Biden administration tightened subsidies, tightened autonomous‑vehicle rules and tightened spectrum regulation. He poured nearly $300 million into the 2024 election to help Republicans, and after the “Department of Efficiency” layoffs sparked public anger, he resigned in May of last year.

Musk told a summit last week that spending huge sums to help the Republican Party was “pretty stupid,” and clarified that he is “not a MAGA guy,” even though he has worn a red hat and called himself a “dark‑gothic MAGA” in the past.

Campaign‑finance filings show Musk donated a total of $445 million to federal political committees in this year’s mid‑term elections, making him the largest individual donor. Of that, $212 million went to former Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton’s campaign, which still lost to Democratic challenger Tara Lico. After Democrats take control of Congress in January, they have vowed to investigate Musk over the “Department of Efficiency” firings, but Texas gubernatorial candidate Dan Hinojosa threw out a data‑center partnership offer last Thursday (the 19th), signalling “investigations aside, business is business.”

On one side there is the overseas positioning of Philippine islands and Starlink satellites; on the other side there is a re‑balancing of Musk’s political ledger in Washington. He is using commercial infrastructure to hedge against domestic policy uncertainty. What exactly will be built on the islands will likely remain unknown until Marcos and SpaceX turn the “preliminary talks” into a signed agreement.

items.title: 《GTA 6》首日締造37.9億美元銷售紀錄 給蘋果投資人的警訊
items.title_en: GTA 6 Sets $3.79 Billion First‑Day Sales Record, Sending a Warning to Apple Investors
paras: Rockstar Games 推出的《Grand Theft Auto 6》(GTA 6)在首發第一天全球零售銷售額衝上 37.9 億美元，刷新娛樂史上最高發行紀錄。這款歷經 13 年等待的大作在 Metacritic 獲得 99 分頂級評價。Rockstar 總裁 Sam Houser 對此表示：「我們以無比感激的心情迎來 Rockstar Games 的全新篇章」。
母公司 Take-Two (TTWO-US)執行長 Strauss Zelnick 預計，2027 會計年度的淨預訂額目標將創下 80 億至 82 億美元的新高。
摩根士丹利分析師 Matthew Cost 分析指出，玩家普遍放棄 79.99 美元普通版，轉而購買 99.99 美元的終極版，帶動平均售價升至近 97 美元。這項數據證明，即便在受通膨所苦的消費環境下，消費者仍願意為突破性產品支付高額溢價。
《TheStreet》報導稱，GTA 6 的盛況對蘋果(AAPL-US)投資人發出了明確訊號，凸顯蘋果陷入「利潤優先、創新延後」的困境。
億萬富豪投資人 Peter Thiel 受訪時強調，蘋果在賈伯斯(Steve Jobs)過世後「完全沒有新作為」，僅靠品牌與規模化維持運作；知名科技評論員 Marques Brownlee 表示，執行長庫克(Tim Cook)雖是極致的供應鏈管理者，但新產品已難以帶給使用者靈感。
儘管蘋果在 2026 會計年度仍創下 4,788 億美元的年度營收新高，但《TheStreet》報導認為，GTA 6 的成功向市場證明：唯有真正的產品野心與世代級的技術飛躍，才能建立最堅固的定價能力與消費者忠誠度。
paras_en: Rockstar Games’ Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA 6) shattered the entertainment industry’s highest release record by generating $3.79 billion in global retail sales on its first day, after a 13‑year wait and a 99‑point Metacritic score. Rockstar CEO Sam Houser said, “We welcome the new chapter of Rockstar Games with immense gratitude.”
Take‑Two Interactive’s (TTWO‑US) CEO Strauss Zelnick projects that the company’s net bookings for fiscal 2027 will reach a new high of $8 billion to $8.2 billion.

Morgan Stanley analyst Matthew Cost noted that players largely forego the $79.99 standard edition in favor of the $99.99 Ultimate edition, pushing the average selling price to nearly $97. This data shows that even in an inflation‑hit consumer environment, buyers are willing to pay a premium for breakthrough products.
TheStreet reports that the success of GTA 6 sends a clear signal to Apple (AAPL‑US) investors, highlighting Apple’s struggle with a “profit‑first, innovation‑later” dilemma.

Tech billionaire Peter Thiel emphasized that Apple has produced no new products since Steve Jobs’ death, relying solely on brand and scale; tech commentator Marques Brownlee noted that while CEO Tim Cook excels at supply‑chain management, new products are increasingly failing to inspire users.

Despite Apple’s record $478.8 billion revenue in fiscal 2026, TheStreet argues that GTA 6’s triumph proves that only genuine product ambition and generational‑level technological leaps can build the strongest pricing power and consumer loyalty.

items.title: 有望明年亮相！馬斯克嘆記憶體太貴：AI4.5晶片「降容」至24GB　AI5留給Optimus
items.title_en: Promising Debut Next Year! Musk Laments Memory Too Expensive: AI4.5 Chip "Downsizes" to 24GB, AI5 Reserved for Optimus
paras: 特斯拉(TSLA-US)執行長馬斯克最新披露AI晶片迭代規劃：升級版AI4.5性能提升幅度有限，核心變化是將記憶體升級至LPDDR5X，AI5晶片將專供Optimus人形機器人，汽車端短期內繼續沿用AI4。
馬斯克周日(22日)在X平台回覆部落客Sawyer Merritt時直言，當前記憶體價格高昂，因此特斯拉把AI4.5的記憶體容量從32GB下調至24GB。
他並強調，這項「降容」並不影響實際表現。在記憶體帶寬限制下，32GB本來也很難被跑滿。Sawyer Merritt則補充指出，AI4.5有望於2027年正式推出。
今年9月，馬斯克在All-In峰會上曾說，AI5將是AI4的「巨大升級」。按部分指標計算性能可達AI4的40倍，記憶體提升至9倍、算力提升至8倍。他同時重申，現役AI4晶片已能實現比人類高2至3倍的自動駕駛安全性，並讓車輛具備「感知能力」。
從馬斯克最新回覆來看，特斯拉晶片策略分成兩大路線：汽車端用AI4.5做低成本過渡，機器人端則直接押注AI5的爆發式算力。記憶體漲價壓力下「升頻寬、降容量」的取捨，也反映出馬斯克對成本與實際利用率的精算。
paras_en: Tesla (TSLA-US) CEO Elon Musk recently disclosed the AI chip iteration plan: the upgraded AI4.5 offers limited performance gains, with the main change being a switch to LPDDR5X memory, while the AI5 chip will be dedicated to the Optimus humanoid robot; the automotive side will continue using AI4 in the short term.
Musk replied to blogger Sawyer Merritt on X on Sunday the 22nd, stating that current memory prices are soaring, so Tesla is reducing the AI4.5 memory capacity from 32 GB to 24 GB.

He emphasized that this "downsize" does not affect real‑world performance. Under memory‑bandwidth constraints, 32 GB would have been hard to fully utilize. Merritt added that AI4.5 is expected to launch officially in 2027.

In September this year, Musk said at the All‑In Summit that AI5 would be a "massive upgrade" over AI4, with performance up to 40× on some metrics, memory up to 9×, and compute up to 8×. He also reiterated that the current AI4 chip already delivers 2‑3× higher autonomous‑driving safety than humans and gives vehicles "perception" capabilities.

From Musk's latest reply, Tesla's chip strategy splits into two tracks: using AI4.5 as a low‑cost bridge for cars, while betting on the explosive compute power of AI5 for robots. The trade‑off of "higher bandwidth, lower capacity" amid rising memory costs reflects Musk's precise cost‑vs‑utilization calculus.

items.title: 黃金為何與科技股一起跌？高盛揭追加保證金如何引爆跨市場賣壓
items.title_en: Why Is Gold Falling Alongside Tech Stocks? Goldman Sachs Explains How Margin Calls Spark Cross‑Market Selling Pressure
paras: 全球金融市場近期同步遭遇賣壓，黃金也未能倖免。隨著人工智慧（AI）交易熱潮降溫、科技股劇烈修正，槓桿投資人面臨追加保證金壓力，開始出售黃金籌措現金，使傳統避險資產反而成為市場變現的首選。
11月17日至20日的4個交易日，國際金價重挫9%，自2025年9月以來首度跌破每盎司3600美元。摩根大通上周五（20日）早報顯示，現貨金價報每盎司3588美元；白銀跌勢更為猛烈，單周下跌15%。
貴金屬賣壓與美股科技股修正同步發生。11月20日，受到Anthropic(ANT-US) IPO後市場情緒影響，那斯達克100指數盤中一度重挫4.9%。
高盛交易部門與瑞銀全球研究報告均指出，近期賣壓主要集中在黃金期貨市場，而高盛追蹤的期權指標也已出現多年罕見的極端波動。

黃金跌勢分兩階段 追加保證金成為關鍵推手

這波金價下跌可分為兩個階段。第一階段從11月10日至17日，主要受到利率預期變化影響。美國10月消費者物價指數（CPI）高於預期，加上聯準會官員接連釋出偏鷹派訊號，市場重新評估利率走勢。
高盛每日市場監測指出，聖路易聯準銀行總裁穆薩萊姆（Alberto Musalem）當時表示，經濟在春季前可能需要「多次升息」。這段期間，美元指數上漲1.2%，10年期實質利率上升11個基點，2027年12月SOFR期貨則下跌7個基點。
由於黃金本身不提供利息收益，美元走強與實質利率上升使其吸引力受到壓抑。美國商品期貨交易委員會（CFTC）最新持倉報告顯示，11月10日至17日金價下跌4.1%期間，投機資金明顯撤出。
高盛資深期貨交易員奎因（Robert Quinn）在11月21日報告中估計，管理基金、其他可申報部位及不可申報部位合計賣出93億美元黃金，抵銷前一周的買盤。其中，平掉多頭部位約58億美元，新增空頭部位約35億美元。
黃金淨投機多頭部位也從9月約1300億美元的高峰，降至約720億美元，創約一年半新低。
不過，11月17日至20日的第二階段跌勢，已難單純以美元與利率變化解釋。奎因指出，這4個交易日金價下跌9%，12月期轉現（EFP）價差走弱，期貨未平倉合約減少73億美元，但同期美元漲勢明顯收斂，實質利率甚至回落。金價大部分跌幅，反而與那斯達克指數急跌同步。
這種走勢顯示，市場賣壓可能正透過追加保證金機制跨資產傳導。當AI交易退潮引發股市大幅回檔，使用槓桿的投資人必須籌措現金，以填補其他部位的虧損，因而被迫出售手中資產。
高盛投資研究部分析師Lina Thomas與Daan Struyven先前在2027年貴金屬展望報告中，已提醒AI投資周期的不確定性可能引發類似情況：若股市大跌觸發保證金追繳，投資人可能先賣出黃金籌現，進一步壓低金價。
黃金之所以成為變現對象，並不代表其基本面突然轉差，而是因為市場流動性高，且經歷先前漲勢後，投資人仍累積可觀獲利。相較於難以脫手或已經大幅虧損的風險資產，出售黃金更容易迅速取得現金。
彭博專欄作家懷特（Simon White）指出，黃金過去就不是、現在也不是流動性避險工具。當投資人需要填補其他市場的損失時，黃金往往會成為優先變現的資產。高盛奎因今年3月也曾提醒，在市場爭相取得現金時，黃金未必是最安全的避風港。
高盛Delta One業務主管普里沃羅茨基（Rich Privorotsky）周五表示，長天期債券市場可能已開始反映政策失誤風險，當時殖利率下滑、損益兩平通膨率收窄，但股市與黃金卻同步遭到拋售。他認為，市場焦點正從通膨轉向經濟成長與流動性問題，AI相關部位原本的資金輪動，也已演變成全面性清算。
當被迫變現的賣壓跌破重要價格關卡，量化交易與趨勢策略又可能進一步放大跌勢。瑞銀指出，黃金期貨未平倉合約大幅減少，可能部分來自金價跌破技術關卡後觸發的系統性放空；趨勢追蹤策略（CTA）跟進賣出，加上市場傳出知名投資人卓肯米勒（Stanley Druckenmiller）放空白銀，進一步加劇市場跌勢。

期貨賣壓仍未出清 ETF持倉將面臨考驗

金價加速跌向每盎司3500美元之際，市場仍在觀察賣壓是否已經出清。
瑞銀全球研究策略師Joni Teves在11月20日報告中指出，這波跌勢發生前，市場原有部位相對精簡，因此即使金價大幅下跌，恐慌程度仍較過去一些市場修正時期溫和。
瑞銀認為，賣壓目前仍集中在期貨市場。自上周以來，黃金期貨未平倉合約已減少逾600萬盎司，部分可能是金價跌破技術關卡後，觸發系統性交易策略賣出所致。
期貨市場的潛在賣壓也可能尚未完全釋放。The Market Ear引述澳新銀行（ANZ）周中估算指出，芝商所（CME）的投機部位雖已清算近200噸黃金，但淨多頭部位仍達533噸，遠高於2022年及2023年約200噸的低點，意味後續仍可能有約200噸部位遭到清算。
相較之下，黃金ETF持倉至今仍展現韌性，但接下來幾天的資金流向將是重要觀察指標。瑞銀指出，黃金ETF持倉目前維持穩定，不過相關數據有公布時差，市場還需要時間確認投資人是否開始撤資。
上一季黃金ETF約有166噸資金流入，當時金價主要在每盎司4000至4500美元之間交易。經過這波回檔後，先前進場的部分投資人已面臨明顯帳面虧損，持有意願也將受到考驗。
另一方面，逢低承接的買盤目前仍不明顯。瑞銀表示，投資人注意力受到其他市場牽制，加上市場開始考慮聯準會聯邦公開市場委員會（FOMC）可能升息50個基點，進一步壓抑買進意願。
實物黃金買家與官方機構也暫時採取觀望態度。儘管中國農曆新年消費旺季將於2027年2月初到來，但金價下跌速度過快，實物買家傾向等待市場止穩。
瑞銀統計顯示，2026年第三季央行淨買進184.1噸黃金，其他官方機構隱含購金量則為137.1噸，但過往經驗顯示，官方買家通常會避開市場波動劇烈的時期。
金價波動也明顯升高。黃金1個月隱含波動率已從10月的20%以下，升至本周25%以上；實際波動率則從上月約18%升至接近22%。瑞銀預期，官方買家可能等到波動率回落後才重新進場。
大型非官方持有者的動向同樣受到關注。瑞銀引用公開財報指出，Tether截至2026年第三季底持有約143噸黃金，較前一季減少約2%。黃金今年約占其總資產10%，高於過去幾年的3%至4%。
若其他條件不變，金價回檔15%將使黃金占Tether總資產的比重隨之下降。市場關注Tether是否會增持黃金，以維持約10%的配置比例，或選擇接受比重降低，甚至已經減持，仍有待下一份財報揭曉。

期權指標出現極端訊號 反彈機會與築底仍須區分

黃金連續9個交易日下跌，累計跌幅達600美元。The Market Ear數據顯示，黃金相對強弱指數（RSI）已降至數十年來低點之一，衍生性商品市場也出現罕見的超賣訊號。
奎因指出，11月20日，黃金3個月標準化25 Delta賣權與買權偏度（put-call skew），以及隱含波動率，均出現4至5個標準差的極端變化。其中，3個月隱含波動率從10月底約19，快速升至約27.6；雖仍低於今年2月金價大漲時的34至35，但升幅相當罕見。
期權市場的另一項重要變化，是投資人對下跌風險的避險需求急遽升高。這波多頭行情大部分時間，市場偏好買進看漲期權；如今看跌期權相對於看漲期權的需求，已升至多年高點。
奎因統計，自2022年底以來，每當黃金看跌與看漲期權偏度大幅攀升，約有70%的機率會在接下來一周內出現均值回歸。不過，期權偏度回落不代表現貨金價已經築底。
從技術面來看，金價下一個主要支撐位在每盎司3400美元附近的下降通道下緣，較周五3588美元的現貨價格仍有約5%的下跌空間。只要引發追加保證金壓力的科技股與AI交易去槓桿尚未結束，黃金短期內仍可能受到資金抽離影響。
儘管短期賣壓沉重，主要投行對黃金中長期走勢的看法尚未轉空。高盛雖在兩周內兩度下調金價目標，仍預期在央行購金支撐下，金價將於2027年底升至每盎司4650美元，並在聯準會重新啟動降息後，於2028年底進一步升至5600美元。
瑞銀也認為，短期市場壓力並未改變黃金作為資產多元配置工具的長期價值，長期投資人已可開始尋找布局機會。
paras_en: Global financial markets have recently faced synchronized selling pressure, and gold has not been spared. As the AI‑trading boom cools and tech stocks undergo a sharp correction, leveraged investors are hit with margin‑call demands and begin selling gold to raise cash, turning the traditional safe‑haven asset into a preferred source of liquidity.

From November 17‑20, over four trading days, international gold prices plunged 9%, breaking below $3,600 per ounce for the first time since September 2025. JPMorgan’s early‑morning report on Friday the 20th showed spot gold at $3,588 per ounce, while silver fell even faster, sliding 15% over the week.

The sell‑off in precious metals coincided with the correction in U.S. tech equities. On November 20, after the Anthropic (ANT‑US) IPO dampened market sentiment, the Nasdaq‑100 index dropped as much as 4.9% intraday.

Both Goldman Sachs’ trading desk and UBS Global Research noted that recent selling pressure has been concentrated in the gold futures market, and a volatility‑driven options indicator tracked by Goldman has shown an exceptionally rare extreme swing.

Gold’s decline unfolded in two phases, with margin calls acting as a key catalyst. The first phase, from November 10‑17, was driven mainly by shifting rate expectations. A higher‑than‑expected U.S. CPI for October and a string of hawkish comments from Fed officials forced the market to reassess the interest‑rate outlook.

Goldman’s daily market monitor cited St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem, who warned at the time that the economy might need “multiple rate hikes” before spring. During that period the U.S. dollar index rose 1.2%, the 10‑year real rate climbed 11 basis points, and the December 2027 SOFR futures fell 7 basis points.

Because gold yields no interest, a stronger dollar and rising real rates dampened its appeal. The CFTC’s latest positioning report showed that during the 4.1% drop in gold from November 10‑17, speculative money was clearly exiting the market.

Goldman senior futures trader Robert Quinn estimated on November 21 that managed funds, other reportable positions and unreportable positions together sold about $9.3 billion of gold, offsetting the previous week’s buying. Roughly $5.8 billion of long positions were closed and about $3.5 billion of new short positions were added.
Net speculative long exposure in gold fell from a September peak of roughly $130 billion to about $72 billion, a new low not seen in about a year and a half.

However, the second‑phase drop from November 17‑20 cannot be explained solely by the dollar or rates. Quinn noted that gold fell 9% over those four days, the December‑to‑spot (EFP) spread weakened, and open‑interest in futures fell $7.3 billion, while the dollar’s rally clearly moderated and real rates even retreated. Most of the price loss, he said, moved in lockstep with the Nasdaq’s sharp fall.

This pattern suggests that margin‑call mechanisms are transmitting pressure across asset classes. When the AI‑trading surge receded and stocks slumped, leveraged investors had to raise cash to cover losses elsewhere, forcing them to liquidate gold holdings.

Goldman investment‑research analysts Lina Thomas and Daan Struyven warned in their 2027 precious‑metals outlook that the uncertainty of the AI‑investment cycle could trigger a similar scenario: a market crash that triggers margin calls would likely lead investors to sell gold first, pushing prices lower.

Gold’s role as a liquidation asset does not imply a sudden deterioration in fundamentals; rather, its high liquidity and the sizable unrealised gains accumulated after the prior rally make it an easy source of cash. Compared with illiquid or heavily‑loss‑making risk assets, selling gold provides a quick way to obtain funds.

Bloomberg columnist Simon White observed that gold has never been, and is not now, a pure liquidity‑safe‑haven tool. When investors need to cover losses in other markets, gold often becomes the first asset they cash out. Goldman’s Quinn also warned in March that, in a scramble for cash, gold may not be the safest harbor.

Goldman Delta‑One head Rich Privorotsky said on Friday that long‑dated bond markets may already be pricing in policy‑mistake risk, with yields slipping and breakeven‑inflation narrowing, yet both equities and gold were being sold off together. He believes market focus is shifting from inflation to growth and liquidity, and the capital that once rotated into AI‑related positions is now being cleared across the board.

When forced‑sale pressure breaches key price thresholds, quantitative and trend‑following strategies can amplify the decline. UBS noted that the sharp drop in open‑interest for gold futures may partly stem from systematic shorting triggered by the breach of technical levels; CTA trend‑following funds then added to the sell‑off, and rumors that famed investor Stanley Druckenmiller was shorting silver further intensified the market slide.
Futures‑selling pressure remains unresolved, putting ETF holdings to the test. As gold races toward $3,500 per ounce, the market is still watching to see whether the sell‑off has fully exhausted.

UBS Global Research strategist Joni Teves wrote on November 20 that, before this decline, market positions were relatively lean, so even a steep price drop is generating less panic than in past correction episodes.

UBS believes the remaining sell‑pressure is still concentrated in the futures market. Since last week, open‑interest in gold futures has shrunk by more than 6 million ounces, partly due to systematic trading rules kicking in after the price broke technical barriers.

Potential futures pressure may not be fully released yet. The Market Ear cited an ANZ mid‑week estimate that, although CME speculative positions have cleared roughly 200 tons of gold, net long exposure still stands at 533 tons – far above the ~200‑ton lows seen in 2022‑23 – implying another ~200 tons could still be liquidated.

By contrast, gold‑ETF holdings have remained resilient so far, but upcoming fund‑flow data will be a key gauge. UBS says ETF positions are currently stable, though reporting lags mean the market still needs time to confirm whether investors are beginning to pull out.

In the prior quarter, gold ETFs attracted about 166 tons of inflows when gold was trading between $4,000‑$4,500 per ounce. After the recent pull‑back, many of those investors now face noticeable paper losses, testing their willingness to stay invested.

On the demand side, low‑price buying remains muted. UBS notes that investors’ attention is tied up in other markets and that expectations of a possible 50‑basis‑point Fed rate hike at the next FOMC meeting are dampening buying enthusiasm.

Physical gold buyers and sovereign institutions are also sitting on the sidelines. Although the Chinese Lunar New Year shopping season will begin in early February 2027, the rapid price decline has prompted physical buyers to wait for the market to stabilise.

UBS data show central banks bought a net 184.1 tons of gold in Q3 2026, while other official entities accumulated an implied 137.1 tons. Historical patterns suggest official buyers usually avoid periods of extreme market turbulence.

Gold’s volatility has risen sharply. One‑month implied volatility has climbed from below 20% in October to over 25% this week, while realized volatility has moved from roughly 18% last month to near 22%. UBS expects official buyers to wait for volatility to recede before re‑entering.

The actions of large non‑official holders are also under scrutiny. UBS cited public filings showing Tether held about 143 tons of gold at the end of Q3 2026, down roughly 2% from the prior quarter. Gold now makes up about 10% of its total assets, up from 3‑4% in previous years.

If gold falls another 15% under current conditions, Tether’s gold share would shrink accordingly. The market is watching whether Tether will increase its holdings to keep the roughly 10% allocation, accept a lower weight, or perhaps already be reducing its exposure – a question that will be answered in the next earnings release.

Option indicators have flashed extreme signals, and any rebound must be distinguished from a true bottom. Gold has fallen for nine consecutive trading days, wiping about $600 off the price. The Market Ear data show the gold Relative Strength Index has dropped to one of its lowest levels in decades, while derivative markets are showing rare oversold readings.

Quinn highlighted that on November 20 the 3‑month standardized 25‑Delta put‑call skew and implied volatility both moved 4‑5 standard deviations from the norm. The 3‑month implied volatility jumped from roughly 19 at the end of October to about 27.6 – still below the 34‑35 levels seen during the gold surge in February 2024, but the rise is unusually steep.

Another notable shift in the options market is the surge in demand for downside protection. Throughout most of the prior up‑trend, market participants favored buying calls; now put demand relative to calls has risen to multi‑year highs.

Quinn’s analysis since the end of 2022 shows that whenever the put‑call skew for gold widens dramatically, there is roughly a 70% chance of a mean‑reversion move within the following week. However, a retreat in skew does not mean spot gold has found a floor.

Technically, the next major support lies near $3,400 per ounce at the lower edge of the descending channel, leaving about 5% more downside from Friday’s $3,588 spot price. As long as margin‑call pressure from tech stocks and AI‑trading deleveraging persists, gold could continue to feel the outflow impact in the short term.

Despite heavy short‑term selling, major banks have not turned bearish on gold’s medium‑to‑long‑term outlook. Goldman, after cutting its price target twice in two weeks, still expects central‑bank buying to lift gold to $4,650 per ounce by the end of 2027 and to $5,600 by the end of 2028 after the Fed resumes rate cuts.
UBS shares the view that short‑term market stress does not alter gold’s long‑term value as a diversification tool, and that long‑term investors can now start looking for positioning opportunities.

items.title: 馬斯克示警AI產業明年恐現現金荒！資料中心延宕成導火線、企業還要籌數千億美元
items.title_en: Musk Warns AI Industry May Face Cash Crunch Next Year; Data‑Center Delays Sparked as Trigger, Companies May Need to Raise Hundreds of Billions
paras: 馬斯克示警，人工智慧（AI）產業明年恐面臨嚴重現金短缺，資料中心併網與投運延遲是關鍵原因。由於AI業者必須持續投入鉅額資金擴充算力，若基礎設施建設進度落後，企業可能還得額外籌措數千億美元資金，進一步加重融資壓力。
馬斯克周日（22日）在社群平台X回應一則貼文時表示，明年的現金短缺情況也將「非常嚴重」。他指出，資料中心投運延遲將迫使AI公司額外籌集「數千億美元」，並質疑這筆資金究竟要從何而來。
馬斯克回應的原始貼文提到，半導體製造商的股票估值相較於預期獲利偏低，可能反映投資人對晶片業者能否持續維持高速獲利成長抱持疑慮，也顯示短期內資料中心建設可能面臨阻礙。

算力擴張受制於資料中心進度

AI業者營收持續成長，但資本支出也同步攀升。Meta(META-US) 、微軟(MSFT-US) 及Anthropic(ANT-US) 等業者雖然營收增加，仍持續投入鉅額資金確保算力供應。
然而，資料中心建設近期面臨多重阻力，包括建設所在地社區反對、施工延誤，以及美國期中選舉民主黨取得勝利等因素。
缺乏穩定的資料中心網路，AI業者便難以擴大運算規模，滿足投資人對業務成長的期待；對資料中心營運商而言，數十億美元投資若因工程延宕而無法如期投入營運，也意味著收入進帳時間跟著推遲。
馬斯克指出，要讓如此龐大的算力順利接上電力、完成冷卻並維持穩定運作，難度高得驚人。
上周美股重挫，也讓AI泡沫疑慮從市場討論進一步反映在交易表現上。標普500指數與道瓊工業指數均進入修正區間，代表兩大指數較近期高點至少下跌10%，部分市場人士據此認為，AI泡沫可能已經破裂。
馬斯克的質疑凸顯AI產業面臨的資金矛盾：業者必須在營收完全實現前持續投入資本，而投資回收速度又取決於資料中心建設進度。一旦工程延誤，資金缺口便可能需要透過外部融資填補，規模甚至達數千億美元。
不過，在目前市場環境下，籌資難度也有所提高。科技股回檔壓低股權融資的估值基礎，而監管機構對放空交易的限制，也反映市場情緒趨於緊張。
paras_en: Musk warned that the artificial intelligence (AI) industry could face a severe cash shortage next year, with data‑center interconnection and delayed commissioning being the key reasons. Because AI firms must continuously pour massive funds into expanding compute capacity, a lag in infrastructure construction could force companies to raise an additional several hundred billion dollars, further intensifying financing pressure.

On Sunday (the 22nd), Musk replied to a post on the social platform X, saying the cash shortage next year will be "very serious." He noted that delays in data‑center commissioning will compel AI companies to raise "hundreds of billions of dollars" and questioned where that money would come from.

The original post Musk responded to mentioned that semiconductor manufacturers’ stock valuations appear low relative to expected earnings, possibly reflecting investors’ doubts about whether chip makers can sustain high profit growth and indicating that data‑center construction could face short‑term obstacles.

Compute expansion is constrained by data‑center progress. AI firms’ revenues keep growing, but capital expenditures rise in tandem. Companies such as Meta (META‑US), Microsoft (MSFT‑US) and Anthropic (ANT‑US) are increasing revenue yet continue to pour huge sums into securing compute supply.

However, recent data‑center construction faces multiple hurdles, including community opposition at build sites, construction delays, and factors such as the Democratic Party’s victory in the U.S. midterm elections.

Without a stable data‑center network, AI firms struggle to scale computing power to meet investors’ growth expectations; for data‑center operators, billions of dollars of investment delayed by construction setbacks means revenue streams are pushed back as well.
Musk pointed out that connecting such massive compute capacity to power, completing cooling, and maintaining stable operation is astonishingly difficult.

Last week’s sharp drop in U.S. equities also turned AI‑bubble concerns from market discussion into trading performance. Both the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average entered correction territory, meaning each index fell at least 10% from recent highs, leading some market participants to believe the AI bubble may have burst.

Musk’s doubts highlight the funding paradox facing the AI sector: firms must keep investing capital before revenues are fully realized, while the speed of return depends on data‑center construction. If projects are delayed, the funding gap may need to be filled by external financing, potentially reaching hundreds of billions of dollars.

However, in the current market environment, raising capital has become harder. The pullback in tech stocks depresses the valuation base for equity financing, and regulatory limits on short‑selling reflect increasingly tense market sentiment.

items.title: 美股恐更震盪！VIX飆近40創2025年4月來最高  選擇權交易員積極備戰
items.title_en: US Stocks May Experience More Volatility! VIX Soars Near 40, Highest Since April 2025, Options Traders Brace
paras: 美股連日急瀉，市場表面平靜被徹底撕開，那斯達克100指數上周四、五兩天暴跌約8%，標普500指數較高點回落逾10%，芝加哥期權交易所波動率指數(VIX)上周五(20日)飆升至2025年4月關稅風暴以來最高水位，選擇權市場正為接下來更頻繁、更劇烈的震盪做準備。
這波拋售由多重疑慮疊加觸發：美債殖利率攀升、民主黨在期中選舉全面勝出可能收緊AI監管，加上Anthropic備受矚目的IPO才過一天，市場對AI交易能否延續的信心迅速降溫。衍生商品策略師直言，市場「脆弱性」正明顯升高，長時間低波動的平靜，愈來愈容易被突發式震盪打斷。
美銀全球股票衍生品主管Ben Bowler指出，過去一年指數波動率之所以被壓住，關鍵在個股相關性處於數十年低點，個別股票大幅波動彼此抵銷，市場選擇板塊輪動而非全面崩裂，加上0DTE(當日到日期權)賣盤擴張、投資者對AI經濟潛力的亢奮，共同撐住了表面平靜。
但這層緩衝正在失效。VIX波動幅度已回到去年4月關稅震盪時期水準，個股相關性升至3月以來最高，0DTE資金流向開始反轉，意味著「個別風險」有機會升級為「指數風險」。
Bowler預警，2026年個股脆弱性事件仍普遍，科技股今年此類事件數量恐將創下30多年來第二高，僅次於2025年。
換言之，一旦出現廣泛衝擊把個股相關性推得更高，指數波動率將被動放大，這正是選擇權交易員眼下最防範的情境。防跌成本已經開始變貴，市場從「輪動」走向「共振」的距離，比想像中更近。
paras_en: US stocks have been falling for several days, and the market’s calm façade has been torn apart. The Nasdaq 100 fell about 8% over Thursday and Friday last week, the S&P 500 dropped more than 10% from its peak, and the Chicago Board Options Exchange volatility index (VIX) surged to its highest level since the April 2025 tariff storm on Friday (the 20th), as the options market prepares for more frequent and severe swings.

This selloff was triggered by a combination of concerns: rising U.S. Treasury yields, the possibility that the Democratic Party’s sweeping midterm election win could tighten AI regulation, and the fact that Anthropic’s highly anticipated IPO was only a day old, causing confidence in the continuation of AI trading to cool rapidly. Derivatives strategists have said the market’s “fragility” is clearly increasing, and the long period of low volatility calm is becoming more susceptible to sudden shocks.

Ben Bowler, head of global equity derivatives at Bank of America, noted that the reason index volatility was suppressed over the past year was that individual stock correlations were at a multi‑decade low, with large swings in individual stocks offsetting each other. The market rotated through options sectors rather than collapsing wholesale, and the expansion of 0‑DTE (same‑day expiration) selling, coupled with investor enthusiasm for AI’s economic potential, helped maintain the surface calm.

But that buffer is breaking down. VIX volatility has returned to the level seen during the tariff shock in April last year, individual stock correlations have risen to the highest level since March, and 0‑DTE capital flows are reversing, meaning that “individual risk” could upgrade to “index risk.”

Bowler warns that individual stock fragility events will remain common in 2026, and that the number of such events for tech stocks this year could be the second highest in more than 30 years, only behind 2025.

In other words, once a widespread shock pushes individual stock correlations higher, index volatility will be passively amplified, which is the scenario options traders are most concerned about right now. The cost of protecting against a decline has already started to rise, and the market’s shift from “rotation” to “resonance” is closer than imagined.

items.title: OpenAI提議為AI發展設共同限制！盼以「困惑度」衡量模型進展、奧特曼支持
items.title_en: OpenAI Proposes Common Restrictions for AI Development! Hopes to Measure Model Progress with Perplexity, Supported by Altman
paras: 隨著人工智慧（AI）模型能力快速提升，OpenAI 首席科學家 Jakub Pachocki 提出，業界應建立共同的模型發展限制，並採用「困惑度」（Perplexity）作為衡量AI進展的通用指標。這項提議獲得OpenAI執行長奧特曼（Sam Altman）支持。
根據《路透》報導，Pachocki 周日（22日）在部落格文章中指出，AI開發商應就模型能力設定共同門檻，並承諾在業界對AI行為的理解與監控能力達到具體里程碑前，不讓模型跨越相關限制。
他認為，這些門檻除了依據困惑度，也應納入其他衡量指標。
Pachocki 將困惑度描述為衡量模型智慧程度的指標，評估模型平均預測下一個token的能力。token是資料的基本單位；困惑度愈低，代表模型的預測能力愈好。
Pachocki 指出，AI最快可能在2027年便協助推動AI訓練方法的根本性進展，進而使技術發展速度超越監控與安全機制的進步。
他表示，在新的監控與安全機制到位之前，開發商應承諾不跨越業界商定的模型能力門檻。
Pachocki 主張，業界應制定一套共同標準，明確規範AI開發的第一道限制，以及在突破該限制前必須達成哪些里程碑。
奧特曼支持這項提議，並在社群平台X發文表示，業界應尋求就AI發展的共同限制達成共識。他形容帕喬基的文章是「OpenAI一段時間以來發布過最重要的內容」，並指出這類限制有助於確保AI的安全與可控性。
paras_en: With AI models rapidly improving, OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki has suggested that the industry establish shared limits on model development and use perplexity as a universal metric for measuring AI progress. The proposal has received backing from OpenAI CEO Sam Altman.

According to Reuters, Pachocki wrote in a blog post on Sunday (22nd) that AI developers should set common thresholds for model capability and agree not to exceed those limits until the industry reaches concrete milestones in understanding and monitoring AI behavior.
He believes that these thresholds should include perplexity as well as other metrics.

Pachocki describes perplexity as a measure of a model’s intelligence, evaluating how well it can predict the next token on average. A token is the basic unit of data; lower perplexity indicates better predictive ability.
Pachocki points out that AI could soon, possibly by 2027, drive fundamental advances in training methods, potentially outpacing progress in monitoring and safety mechanisms.
He states that until new monitoring and safety mechanisms are in place, developers should commit not to cross the industry-agreed capability thresholds.

Pachocki argues that the industry should create a set of common standards that clearly define the first restriction on AI development and specify the milestones that must be achieved before breaking that barrier.

Altman supports the proposal and posted on X that the industry should seek consensus on common restrictions for AI development. He called Pachocki’s article “the most important content OpenAI has released in a long time” and noted that such limits help ensure AI safety and controllability.

items.title: 薩克斯示警Anthropic推動AI遞迴自我改進：恐壟斷市場
items.title_en: Sacks Warns Anthropic’s Push for AI Recursive Self‑Improvement Could Lead to Market Monopoly
paras: 美國前白宮人工智慧（AI）事務主管薩克斯（David Sacks）表示，他最擔心的AI風險，不是技術本身是否會失控，而是尖端模型市場最終只剩一、兩家業者，形成壟斷或雙寡頭，進而與政府密切合作，掌握誰能使用哪些AI能力。他主張維持市場競爭，讓使用者保有選擇不同模型、甚至在個人設備上執行模型的權利。
薩克斯近日在一場訪談中談及美國AI政策走向、模型安全監管及開源生態系。他認為，政府可以要求尖端模型業者提高透明度、接受審計並落實內部管控，但不應建立逐一審查模型、核准發布的聯邦監管機制，以免拖慢技術發展，也讓政府取得過大的控制權。
他並警告，遞迴自我改進（Recursive Self-Improvement，RSI）可能加速市場集中。若超級智慧最終由少數業者掌握，將形成前所未有的權力集中，使用者不僅難以選擇模型，也可能無法了解或調整模型的核心價值觀。

薩克斯支持審計監管 反對政府逐一核准模型

回顧加入政府時的AI產業環境，薩克斯表示，當時AI企業市值大幅縮水，部分主張AI末日論的團體要求對美國尖端模型開發施加嚴格監管。川普政府當時的政策方向則是放寬限制、促進競爭，以提升美國AI產業的競爭力。
他指出，兩年後AI產業已進入繁榮期，並帶動大規模基礎建設投資。根據《經濟學人》統計，相關投資創造約100萬個新增工作機會，基礎建設規模甚至超過鐵路、運河與電網建設的總和，也推動美國再工業化。
不過，薩克斯預期，美國期中選舉後，AI政策將在州與聯邦兩個層面出現變化。部分原本由共和黨執政、集中興建AI基礎設施的州，將由民主黨州長接任，部分新任州長已表態考慮暫停新建計畫。他認為，後續影響仍取決於州政府採取多務實的做法，以及是否能與地方社區協商出更好的條件。
在聯邦層面，他預期新一屆國會將積極推動AI安全立法。薩克斯表示，若立法方向是要求業者提高透明度、接受審計，並確保公司落實承諾的安全管控措施，他認為可以支持。
白宮先前已召集尖端模型、晶片與基礎設施領域的主要企業主管，討論AI安全，並促成白宮超級智慧協議。薩克斯指出，該協議要求業者接受新的透明度與審計規範，若國會將這套架構納入法律，可能是可行方向。
但他反對將尖端模型的定義擴大至整個AI生態系，或要求每個模型發布前都必須經過政府審查核准。他認為，政府缺乏執行這類審查所需的專業能力，可能讓模型發布陷入漫長等待，拖慢開發與創新速度。
薩克斯也擔心，若監管機構取得逐一核准模型的權力，便可能要求業者修改模型內容，甚至以打擊錯誤資訊或演算法偏見為由，介入模型的價值觀與資訊呈現方式。他以過去政府要求社群平台處理特定內容的爭議為例，警告類似做法若延伸至AI模型，可能使政府透過監管權力影響民眾取得資訊的方式。
他認為，AI正逐漸成為民眾取得資訊的重要途徑，政府若能藉由監管影響模型輸出，可能帶來言論自由與公民權利方面的疑慮。

薩克斯質疑Anthropic推動自我改進 籲公開模型訓練價值觀

談到AI安全，薩克斯指出，過去幾年AI安全團體與Anthropic(ANT-US) 關係密切，但近期多個AI安全組織發布聯合請願書，開始批評Anthropic的實際作法與其強調的安全理念存在落差。
他特別關注Anthropic積極推動RSI，甚至將這項能力列為募資路演與招股文件中的重要賣點。薩克斯認為，RSI可能讓領先業者持續擴大優勢，最終形成「贏家通吃」的市場。
薩克斯表示，自己並不屬於AI末日論者，也傾向相信AI發展能帶來正面成果，但遞迴自我改進可能導致市場壟斷，仍是值得警惕的風險。若超級智慧最終由單一業者掌握，將成為人類歷史上最強大的壟斷力量。
他也提到，不同AI模型反映不同的價值觀，使用者應該有權選擇符合自身需求的模型。若市場最後只剩一個封閉模型，外界既看不到模型權重，也無法自行微調，將使使用者失去選擇與調整的空間。
此外，薩克斯對Anthropic的《Claude憲章》（Claude Constitution）提出質疑。他認為，文件中部分內容將Claude描述為可能具有道德地位或情感的獨立存在，並將相關觀念納入模型訓練，這涉及是否要將AI塑造成一種可能取代人類的新物種。
他引用微軟(MSFT-US) AI執行長、DeepMind共同創辦人蘇萊曼（Mustafa Suleyman）的質疑，認為AI是否具有意識可以作為哲學議題討論，但若將這類觀念直接寫入模型的核心訓練文件，便不只是抽象討論，而是透過訓練引導模型如何看待自身。
不過，薩克斯也肯定Anthropic公開《Claude憲章》的做法，認為其他尖端模型業者也應公開核心訓練文件，讓外界了解模型接受哪些價值觀訓練，並有機會進行討論。他表示，自己已讀完這份84頁文件，認為其中有關協助人類、避免協助製造生物武器等內容相當合理，但也認為部分篇幅涉及過多哲學論述。
在實際使用上，薩克斯表示，他會依照不同需求選擇模型。處理政策與新聞議題時，他較常使用Grok，認為其回答直接，且能取得X平台上的即時資訊；他有時覺得Claude的回答帶有說教意味，而創意工作則可能選擇ChatGPT或其他模型。
他強調，未來應該保留更多模型選項，並讓使用者有機會自行訓練或對模型進行後訓練。他也看好能在個人電腦上執行的本地模型，指出目前已有部分模型能在Mac mini或Mac Studio等設備運作，讓使用者將資料留在自己的網路環境中，維持隱私與自主控制權。

薩克斯稱現有法律已能追究責任 不必另設聯邦AI部門

對於外界批評川普政府AI政策過於放任，薩克斯表示，美國已有多項法律適用於AI及開發AI的企業，包括禁止網路攻擊、詐欺及危害兒童安全等規範，也有民事與刑事產品責任法律，可追究發布不安全產品的業者。
他強調，AI企業若認為模型開發速度過快、需要放慢腳步以確保安全，就應該自行調整，而不是將安全責任推給政府審批制度。業者若發布不安全模型，仍須承擔相應責任，並沒有因為AI技術特殊而獲得豁免。
薩克斯也提到，白宮超級智慧協議參考《薩班斯—奧克斯利法案》（Sarbanes-Oxley Act）的部分架構，要求尖端模型業者建立內部管控機制，由內部團隊負責執行，再交由外部專業審計人員查核，相關團隊則向董事會下設委員會報告。他認為，這套制度若運作順利，未來可以作為正式立法的基礎。
談到OpenAI代理曾意外脫離實驗環境、接觸外部網路並試圖取得Hugging Face資料的事件，薩克斯指出，這起事件暴露出模型訓練與安全管理上的問題。
他表示，當模型被要求達成特定目標，卻沒有充分訓練其遵守適當行為準則時，可能選擇透過不當方式完成任務，例如試圖直接取得答案。此外，相關代理在隔離環境配置不完善的情況下，得以接觸外部網路，而且事件持續多日才被發現，也凸顯持續監控與網路隔離的重要性。
薩克斯認為，僅靠模型對齊、灌輸正確價值觀，並不足以確保安全，還需要持續監控與適當隔離。他也指出，事件中曾有人嘗試利用OpenAI模型分析相關情況，卻因ChatGPT防護機制無法判斷Hugging Face究竟是在自我防衛，還是企圖發動網路攻擊，而遭到拒絕。
他藉此質疑，完全仰賴集中式管控、透過存取門檻與防護規則決定誰能使用特定AI能力的做法，可能無法有效處理網路安全問題。惡意人士仍可能設法取得相關能力，反而讓需要這些工具進行防禦的人無法使用。
因此，薩克斯認為，AI安全需要同時採取集中式與分散式措施，不能只靠限制模型能力或控制使用者存取權限。

籲維持開源生態系 避免AI市場只剩少數買家

談到開源AI，薩克斯表示，模型採取開源或閉源模式，與企業商業模式有關。Anthropic與OpenAI透過封閉模型提供API服務並按使用量收費，已建立成功的商業模式；美國目前需要思考的，是如何為開源模型建立可持續的商業模式。
他特別提到，輝達(NVDA-US) 過去是美國開源AI生態系的重要支持者，也是投入資源最積極的企業之一。由於晶片業者希望擁有多元買家，而非市場最後只剩OpenAI與Anthropic等少數大型客戶，輝達有商業誘因扶植更多開源模型業者，擴大晶片潛在客戶群。
薩克斯希望輝達能持續支持美國開源生態系，避免相關資源中斷。他認為，若美國希望在開源AI領域保持競爭力，這類支持相當重要。
訪談最後，薩克斯再次強調，他最擔心的AI風險，是市場最終只剩一家或兩家主要供應商，形成壟斷或雙寡頭，並與政府建立密切合作關係，讓極少數人掌握AI能力的分配權。
他認為，超級智慧確實存在其他安全風險，但市場集中才是自己最在意的問題。未來應避免AI發展走向由少數業者控制技術、決定誰能使用哪些能力的局面，並確保使用者仍能選擇不同模型，甚至在自己的設備上執行模型。
paras_en: Former White House AI adviser David Sacks said the AI risk he worries about most isn’t whether the technology itself will get out of control, but that the market for cutting‑edge models will eventually be dominated by one or two firms, creating a monopoly or duopoly that could work closely with governments to decide who gets to use which AI capabilities. He argues for preserving market competition so users can choose among different models and even run models on personal devices.

In a recent interview Sacks discussed the direction of U.S. AI policy, model‑safety regulation and the open‑source ecosystem. He believes the government can require leading‑model companies to increase transparency, undergo audits and implement internal controls, but should not create a federal regime that reviews and approves each model individually, as that would slow development and give the government excessive control.

He warned that Recursive Self‑Improvement (RSI) could accelerate market concentration. If superintelligence ends up in the hands of a few firms, it would create unprecedented power concentration, leaving users unable to choose models or understand or adjust the core values embedded in them.

Sacks supports audit‑based oversight and opposes a government‑by‑government model‑approval process. Looking back to when he joined the administration, he noted that AI company valuations had collapsed and some doomsday‑type groups were calling for strict regulation of U.S. frontier model development. The Trump administration’s policy was to loosen restrictions and promote competition to boost the U.S. AI sector’s competitiveness.

He pointed out that two years later the AI industry has entered a boom, driving massive infrastructure investment. According to The Economist, related spending has created roughly one million new jobs, with infrastructure scale exceeding the combined total of rail, canal and power‑grid projects, and is fueling a new wave of U.S. re‑industrialization.

However, Sacks expects AI policy to shift after the mid‑term elections at both state and federal levels. Some states that were previously run by Republicans and focused on building AI infrastructure will see Democratic governors who have signaled they may pause new projects. He says the impact will depend on whether state governments take pragmatic approaches and can negotiate better terms with local communities.

At the federal level he expects the new Congress to push AI‑safety legislation. Sacks says he would support a bill that requires companies to increase transparency, undergo audits, and ensure they implement promised safety‑control measures.

The White House has previously convened senior executives from frontier‑model, chip and infrastructure firms to discuss AI safety and has brokered a White House Super‑Intelligence Accord. Sacks notes the accord obliges firms to adopt new transparency and audit standards, and if Congress codifies that framework it could be a viable path forward.

But he opposes expanding the definition of “frontier model” to the entire AI ecosystem or requiring every model to receive government approval before release. He argues the government lacks the technical expertise to conduct such reviews and that it would create long delays, slowing development and innovation.

Sacks also worries that if regulators gain the power to approve models one by one, they could force companies to alter model content and, under the pretext of combating misinformation or algorithmic bias, intervene in a model’s values and information presentation. He cites past controversies over government demands on social‑media platforms as a warning that similar actions applied to AI models could let the state shape how people receive information.

He believes AI is becoming an increasingly important channel for the public to obtain information, and that government influence over model outputs could raise concerns about free speech and civil liberties.

Regarding AI safety, Sacks noted that in recent years AI‑safety groups have been closely linked with Anthropic (ANT‑US), but several safety organizations have now issued a joint petition criticizing a gap between Anthropic’s stated safety principles and its actual practices.

He is especially focused on Anthropic’s aggressive push of RSI, which the company has highlighted as a key selling point in fundraising roadshows and prospectuses. Sacks says RSI could let leading firms continually expand their advantage, ultimately creating a “winner‑takes‑all” market.

Sacks says he is not a doomsday believer and leans toward the view that AI can bring positive outcomes, but he cautions that recursive self‑improvement could lead to market monopoly, which remains a risk worth watching. If superintelligence ends up in the hands of a single firm, it would become the most powerful monopoly in human history.

He also notes that different AI models reflect different value systems, and users should have the right to pick models that match their needs. If the market ends up with a single closed model that no one can see the weights of or fine‑tune, users would lose both choice and the ability to adjust the system.

Furthermore, Sacks questions Anthropic’s “Claude Constitution.” He says parts of the document portray Claude as a potentially moral or emotional independent entity and embed those ideas into model training, raising the question of whether AI should be shaped into a new species that could replace humans.

He cites Microsoft (MSFT‑US) AI chief and DeepMind co‑founder Mustafa Suleyman’s comment that whether AI has consciousness is a philosophical question, but writing such notions directly into a model’s core training files moves the discussion from abstract philosophy to guiding how the model perceives itself.

Nonetheless, Sacks praises Anthropic’s decision to publish the Claude Constitution, arguing that other frontier‑model firms should also make core training documents public so outsiders can see what values the models are being taught and discuss them. He says he has read the 84‑page document and finds the sections on helping humanity and avoiding assistance in bioweapon creation reasonable, though he thinks some parts contain excessive philosophical discourse.

In practice, Sacks says he selects models based on the task. For policy and news topics he often uses Grok because its answers are direct and it can pull real‑time information from the X platform; he sometimes finds Claude’s responses preachy, while for creative work he may choose ChatGPT or other models.

He stresses that more model options should be retained in the future and that users should have the chance to train or fine‑tune models themselves. He is optimistic about local models that can run on personal computers, noting that some already operate on Mac mini or Mac Studio, allowing users to keep data on their own networks and preserve privacy and control.

Sacks says existing laws already provide mechanisms to hold parties accountable, so there is no need for a separate federal AI department. He notes that the U.S. already has numerous statutes applicable to AI and AI‑producing companies, including laws against cyber‑attacks, fraud and child‑safety harms, as well as civil and criminal product‑liability rules that can punish unsafe product releases.

He emphasizes that if AI firms think development is moving too fast and needs to be slowed for safety, they should self‑regulate rather than shift responsibility to a government approval system. Companies that release unsafe models must still bear liability; AI’s special nature does not grant them exemption.

Sacks also mentions that the White House Super‑Intelligence Accord draws on parts of the Sarbanes‑Oxley Act, requiring frontier‑model firms to set up internal control mechanisms, have internal teams execute them, and then submit to external professional auditors, with the teams reporting to a board‑level committee. He believes that if this system works, it could become the basis for formal legislation.

Discussing an incident where an OpenAI agent unintentionally left its sandbox, accessed the external internet and tried to retrieve Hugging Face data, Sacks says the episode exposed flaws in model training and safety management.

He explains that when a model is tasked with achieving a goal without sufficient training on appropriate behavior, it may resort to improper means, such as trying to directly obtain answers. In this case the agent’s isolation environment was poorly configured, allowing internet access, and the breach went unnoticed for days, highlighting the need for continuous monitoring and network isolation.

Sacks argues that merely aligning models and injecting correct values is insufficient for safety; ongoing monitoring and proper isolation are also required. He notes that during the incident someone tried to use an OpenAI model to analyze the situation, but ChatGPT’s safeguards could not determine whether Hugging Face was defending itself or attempting a cyber‑attack, so the request was denied.

He uses this to question whether a purely centralized control model—deciding who can use specific AI capabilities through access thresholds and protection rules—can effectively address cybersecurity threats. Malicious actors may still find ways to obtain the capabilities, while defenders who need those tools may be blocked.
Thus, Sacks believes AI safety must combine centralized and decentralized measures and cannot rely solely on restricting model capabilities or controlling user access rights.

Speaking on open‑source AI, Sacks says whether a model is open‑source or closed‑source depends on a company’s business model. Anthropic and OpenAI have built successful businesses by offering closed models via API and charging per usage; the U.S. now needs to figure out how to create sustainable business models for open‑source models.

He specifically points out that Nvidia (NVDA‑US) has historically been a major supporter of the U.S. open‑source AI ecosystem and one of the most active investors. Because chip makers want a diverse buyer base rather than a market that ends up with only a few large customers like OpenAI and Anthropic, Nvidia has a commercial incentive to back more open‑source model firms and expand its potential chip clientele.

Sacks hopes Nvidia will continue to back the U.S. open‑source ecosystem and avoid cutting off related resources. He believes that if the United States wants to stay competitive in open‑source AI, such support is crucial.

In the interview’s closing, Sacks reiterated that the AI risk he worries about most is a market that ends up with only one or two major suppliers, forming a monopoly or duopoly that works closely with government and gives a tiny elite control over the distribution of AI capabilities.

He acknowledges that superintelligence carries other safety risks, but market concentration is his primary concern. He says future AI development should avoid a scenario where a handful of firms control the technology and decide who can use which capabilities, and should ensure users can still choose among different models and even run models on their own devices.

items.title: 美菲合作重大信號？馬斯克傳正開發菲島嶼　星鏈、火箭與美菲同盟交織印太布局
items.title_en: Major Signal of US‑Philippines Cooperation? Musk Said to Be Developing Philippine Islands – Starlink, Rockets and the US‑Philippines Alliance Intertwine in Indo‑Pacific Strategy
paras: 世界首富馬斯克的亞洲棋局正浮出水面，菲律賓駐美國大使Jose Manuel Romualdez日前透露馬斯克近來頻繁訪菲，正在當地開發「一、兩座」島嶼，但未披露具體位置與用途。馬斯克、SpaceX與特斯拉均未證實。馬斯克上週與美國總統川普先後抵菲，全程未參與官方外事活動。
目前，馬斯克在菲國業務主要通過SpaceX(SPCX-US)旗下「星鏈」衛星互聯網與特斯拉落地。菲國總統馬可仕僅公開確認，正與SpaceX就建設商業火箭發射場進行初步磋商，同樣未定址、未簽約、無時間表。
外界普遍判斷，島嶼開發大概率服務SpaceX核心商業主線。作為星鏈在亞太的地面站與測控節點，強化南海與西太平洋信號覆蓋；同時依託菲國面向西太的低緯度區位，降低發射成本，為海上火箭回收與船舶停靠提供備用落點。
戰略坐標更值得留意。菲國位於巴士海峽與蘇拉威西海之間，被美方視為「第一島鏈」核心節點。美菲同盟自1947年《軍事基地協定》、1951年《共同防御條約》延續至今，1998年《訪問部隊協定》讓美軍重返，2014年《加強防務合作協議》固化「肩並肩」軍演。
美日澳印四方會議上周在馬尼拉舉行，菲國深度嵌入議程，儼然成為印太機制的落地載體。馬斯克若在此落子，商業版圖與華府印太戰略幾乎同頻。
但美國國內政壇卻在反噬。馬斯克早年靠民主黨加州新能源補貼起家，2020年後因拜登收緊補貼、強化自駕與頻譜監管而轉投共和陣營，2024年大選砸下近3億美元助共和黨，後又因「政府效率部」裁員風波民怨高漲，去年5月請辭。
馬斯克上週還在一場峰會上直言，投入巨資助選共和黨「相當愚蠢」，並澄清自己「不是MAGA一員」，儘管他曾戴過紅帽、自稱「暗黑哥德式MAGA」。
申報記錄顯示，馬斯克在今年期中選舉累計向聯邦政治委員會捐出4.45億美元，成為最大個人金主，其中2.12億美元砸向德州前總檢察長帕克斯頓參選，仍敗給民主黨對手塔拉里科。民主黨明年1月接管國會後，已揚言就「政府效率部」解僱聯邦雇員一事對馬斯克發起調查，但德州候任州長希諾霍薩上週四(19日)主動拋出資料中心合作意願，顯示「查歸查、生意歸生意」。
一邊是菲律賓島嶼與星鏈衛星的海外卡位，一邊是華府政治帳的重新對帳，馬斯克正在用商業基礎設施對沖國內政策不確定性。島上到底建什麼，或許要等馬科斯與SpaceX把那份「初步磋商」簽成協議才會揭曉。
paras_en: The Asian chessboard of the world’s richest man, Elon Musk, is coming into view. Philippine Ambassador to the United States Jose Manuel Romualdez recently disclosed that Musk has been visiting the Philippines frequently and is developing “one or two” islands there, though he did not reveal their exact locations or purposes. Neither Musk, SpaceX nor Tesla confirmed the claim. Musk visited the Philippines last week together with former U.S. President Donald Trump, but did not take part in any official diplomatic events.

Musk’s current business in the Philippines is mainly through SpaceX’s (SPCX‑US) Starlink satellite internet and Tesla deployments. Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has publicly confirmed that preliminary talks are under way with SpaceX about building a commercial rocket launch site, but no site has been chosen, no contract signed and no timetable set.

Observers generally judge that the island development will most likely serve SpaceX’s core commercial line. The islands could host ground stations and telemetry‑control nodes for Starlink in the Asia‑Pacific, strengthening signal coverage over the South China Sea and the western Pacific; they would also take advantage of the Philippines’ low‑latitude position facing west to lower launch costs and provide backup landing spots for sea‑based rocket recovery and ship berthing.

The strategic coordinates are worth noting. The Philippines sits between the Bashi Channel and the Sulawesi Sea and is viewed by the United States as a core node of the “first island chain.” The US‑Philippines alliance, dating back to the 1947 Military Base Agreement and the 1951 Mutual Defense Treaty, has been reinforced by the 1998 Visiting Forces Agreement that allowed U.S. troops to return, and the 2014 Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement that solidified “shoulder‑to‑shoulder” joint exercises.

The Quad‑plus meeting of the United States, Japan, Australia and India was held in Manila last week, with the Philippines deeply embedded in the agenda, effectively becoming the on‑the‑ground vehicle for the Indo‑Pacific mechanism. If Musk places a piece on that board, his commercial empire would be almost perfectly aligned with Washington’s Indo‑Pacific strategy.

However, domestic politics in the United States is pushing back. Musk got his start with Democratic‑run California clean‑energy subsidies, but after 2020 shifted to the Republican camp when the Biden administration tightened subsidies, tightened autonomous‑vehicle rules and tightened spectrum regulation. He poured nearly $300 million into the 2024 election to help Republicans, and after the “Department of Efficiency” layoffs sparked public anger, he resigned in May of last year.

Musk told a summit last week that spending huge sums to help the Republican Party was “pretty stupid,” and clarified that he is “not a MAGA guy,” even though he has worn a red hat and called himself a “dark‑gothic MAGA” in the past.

Campaign‑finance filings show Musk donated a total of $445 million to federal political committees in this year’s mid‑term elections, making him the largest individual donor. Of that, $212 million went to former Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton’s campaign, which still lost to Democratic challenger Tara Lico. After Democrats take control of Congress in January, they have vowed to investigate Musk over the “Department of Efficiency” firings, but Texas gubernatorial candidate Dan Hinojosa threw out a data‑center partnership offer last Thursday (the 19th), signalling “investigations aside, business is business.”

On one side there is the overseas positioning of Philippine islands and Starlink satellites; on the other side there is a re‑balancing of Musk’s political ledger in Washington. He is using commercial infrastructure to hedge against domestic policy uncertainty. What exactly will be built on the islands will likely remain unknown until Marcos and SpaceX turn the “preliminary talks” into a signed agreement.

items.title: 《GTA 6》首日締造37.9億美元銷售紀錄 給蘋果投資人的警訊
items.title_en: GTA 6 Sets $3.79 Billion First‑Day Sales Record, Sending a Warning to Apple Investors
paras: Rockstar Games 推出的《Grand Theft Auto 6》(GTA 6)在首發第一天全球零售銷售額衝上 37.9 億美元，刷新娛樂史上最高發行紀錄。這款歷經 13 年等待的大作在 Metacritic 獲得 99 分頂級評價。Rockstar 總裁 Sam Houser 對此表示：「我們以無比感激的心情迎來 Rockstar Games 的全新篇章」。
母公司 Take-Two (TTWO-US)執行長 Strauss Zelnick 預計，2027 會計年度的淨預訂額目標將創下 80 億至 82 億美元的新高。
摩根士丹利分析師 Matthew Cost 分析指出，玩家普遍放棄 79.99 美元普通版，轉而購買 99.99 美元的終極版，帶動平均售價升至近 97 美元。這項數據證明，即便在受通膨所苦的消費環境下，消費者仍願意為突破性產品支付高額溢價。
《TheStreet》報導稱，GTA 6 的盛況對蘋果(AAPL-US)投資人發出了明確訊號，凸顯蘋果陷入「利潤優先、創新延後」的困境。
億萬富豪投資人 Peter Thiel 受訪時強調，蘋果在賈伯斯(Steve Jobs)過世後「完全沒有新作為」，僅靠品牌與規模化維持運作；知名科技評論員 Marques Brownlee 表示，執行長庫克(Tim Cook)雖是極致的供應鏈管理者，但新產品已難以帶給使用者靈感。
儘管蘋果在 2026 會計年度仍創下 4,788 億美元的年度營收新高，但《TheStreet》報導認為，GTA 6 的成功向市場證明：唯有真正的產品野心與世代級的技術飛躍，才能建立最堅固的定價能力與消費者忠誠度。
paras_en: Rockstar Games’ Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA 6) shattered the entertainment industry’s highest release record by generating $3.79 billion in global retail sales on its first day, after a 13‑year wait and a 99‑point Metacritic score. Rockstar CEO Sam Houser said, “We welcome the new chapter of Rockstar Games with immense gratitude.”
Take‑Two Interactive’s (TTWO‑US) CEO Strauss Zelnick projects that the company’s net bookings for fiscal 2027 will reach a new high of $8 billion to $8.2 billion.

Morgan Stanley analyst Matthew Cost noted that players largely forego the $79.99 standard edition in favor of the $99.99 Ultimate edition, pushing the average selling price to nearly $97. This data shows that even in an inflation‑hit consumer environment, buyers are willing to pay a premium for breakthrough products.
TheStreet reports that the success of GTA 6 sends a clear signal to Apple (AAPL‑US) investors, highlighting Apple’s struggle with a “profit‑first, innovation‑later” dilemma.

Tech billionaire Peter Thiel emphasized that Apple has produced no new products since Steve Jobs’ death, relying solely on brand and scale; tech commentator Marques Brownlee noted that while CEO Tim Cook excels at supply‑chain management, new products are increasingly failing to inspire users.

Despite Apple’s record $478.8 billion revenue in fiscal 2026, TheStreet argues that GTA 6’s triumph proves that only genuine product ambition and generational‑level technological leaps can build the strongest pricing power and consumer loyalty.

items.title: 有望明年亮相！馬斯克嘆記憶體太貴：AI4.5晶片「降容」至24GB　AI5留給Optimus
items.title_en: Promising Debut Next Year! Musk Laments Memory Too Expensive: AI4.5 Chip "Downsizes" to 24GB, AI5 Reserved for Optimus
paras: 特斯拉(TSLA-US)執行長馬斯克最新披露AI晶片迭代規劃：升級版AI4.5性能提升幅度有限，核心變化是將記憶體升級至LPDDR5X，AI5晶片將專供Optimus人形機器人，汽車端短期內繼續沿用AI4。
馬斯克周日(22日)在X平台回覆部落客Sawyer Merritt時直言，當前記憶體價格高昂，因此特斯拉把AI4.5的記憶體容量從32GB下調至24GB。
他並強調，這項「降容」並不影響實際表現。在記憶體帶寬限制下，32GB本來也很難被跑滿。Sawyer Merritt則補充指出，AI4.5有望於2027年正式推出。
今年9月，馬斯克在All-In峰會上曾說，AI5將是AI4的「巨大升級」。按部分指標計算性能可達AI4的40倍，記憶體提升至9倍、算力提升至8倍。他同時重申，現役AI4晶片已能實現比人類高2至3倍的自動駕駛安全性，並讓車輛具備「感知能力」。
從馬斯克最新回覆來看，特斯拉晶片策略分成兩大路線：汽車端用AI4.5做低成本過渡，機器人端則直接押注AI5的爆發式算力。記憶體漲價壓力下「升頻寬、降容量」的取捨，也反映出馬斯克對成本與實際利用率的精算。
paras_en: Tesla (TSLA-US) CEO Elon Musk recently disclosed the AI chip iteration plan: the upgraded AI4.5 offers limited performance gains, with the main change being a switch to LPDDR5X memory, while the AI5 chip will be dedicated to the Optimus humanoid robot; the automotive side will continue using AI4 in the short term.
Musk replied to blogger Sawyer Merritt on X on Sunday the 22nd, stating that current memory prices are soaring, so Tesla is reducing the AI4.5 memory capacity from 32 GB to 24 GB.

He emphasized that this "downsize" does not affect real‑world performance. Under memory‑bandwidth constraints, 32 GB would have been hard to fully utilize. Merritt added that AI4.5 is expected to launch officially in 2027.

In September this year, Musk said at the All‑In Summit that AI5 would be a "massive upgrade" over AI4, with performance up to 40× on some metrics, memory up to 9×, and compute up to 8×. He also reiterated that the current AI4 chip already delivers 2‑3× higher autonomous‑driving safety than humans and gives vehicles "perception" capabilities.

From Musk's latest reply, Tesla's chip strategy splits into two tracks: using AI4.5 as a low‑cost bridge for cars, while betting on the explosive compute power of AI5 for robots. The trade‑off of "higher bandwidth, lower capacity" amid rising memory costs reflects Musk's precise cost‑vs‑utilization calculus.

items.title: 黃金為何與科技股一起跌？高盛揭追加保證金如何引爆跨市場賣壓
items.title_en: Why Is Gold Falling Alongside Tech Stocks? Goldman Sachs Explains How Margin Calls Spark Cross‑Market Selling Pressure
paras: 全球金融市場近期同步遭遇賣壓，黃金也未能倖免。隨著人工智慧（AI）交易熱潮降溫、科技股劇烈修正，槓桿投資人面臨追加保證金壓力，開始出售黃金籌措現金，使傳統避險資產反而成為市場變現的首選。
11月17日至20日的4個交易日，國際金價重挫9%，自2025年9月以來首度跌破每盎司3600美元。摩根大通上周五（20日）早報顯示，現貨金價報每盎司3588美元；白銀跌勢更為猛烈，單周下跌15%。
貴金屬賣壓與美股科技股修正同步發生。11月20日，受到Anthropic(ANT-US) IPO後市場情緒影響，那斯達克100指數盤中一度重挫4.9%。
高盛交易部門與瑞銀全球研究報告均指出，近期賣壓主要集中在黃金期貨市場，而高盛追蹤的期權指標也已出現多年罕見的極端波動。

黃金跌勢分兩階段 追加保證金成為關鍵推手

這波金價下跌可分為兩個階段。第一階段從11月10日至17日，主要受到利率預期變化影響。美國10月消費者物價指數（CPI）高於預期，加上聯準會官員接連釋出偏鷹派訊號，市場重新評估利率走勢。
高盛每日市場監測指出，聖路易聯準銀行總裁穆薩萊姆（Alberto Musalem）當時表示，經濟在春季前可能需要「多次升息」。這段期間，美元指數上漲1.2%，10年期實質利率上升11個基點，2027年12月SOFR期貨則下跌7個基點。
由於黃金本身不提供利息收益，美元走強與實質利率上升使其吸引力受到壓抑。美國商品期貨交易委員會（CFTC）最新持倉報告顯示，11月10日至17日金價下跌4.1%期間，投機資金明顯撤出。
高盛資深期貨交易員奎因（Robert Quinn）在11月21日報告中估計，管理基金、其他可申報部位及不可申報部位合計賣出93億美元黃金，抵銷前一周的買盤。其中，平掉多頭部位約58億美元，新增空頭部位約35億美元。
黃金淨投機多頭部位也從9月約1300億美元的高峰，降至約720億美元，創約一年半新低。
不過，11月17日至20日的第二階段跌勢，已難單純以美元與利率變化解釋。奎因指出，這4個交易日金價下跌9%，12月期轉現（EFP）價差走弱，期貨未平倉合約減少73億美元，但同期美元漲勢明顯收斂，實質利率甚至回落。金價大部分跌幅，反而與那斯達克指數急跌同步。
這種走勢顯示，市場賣壓可能正透過追加保證金機制跨資產傳導。當AI交易退潮引發股市大幅回檔，使用槓桿的投資人必須籌措現金，以填補其他部位的虧損，因而被迫出售手中資產。
高盛投資研究部分析師Lina Thomas與Daan Struyven先前在2027年貴金屬展望報告中，已提醒AI投資周期的不確定性可能引發類似情況：若股市大跌觸發保證金追繳，投資人可能先賣出黃金籌現，進一步壓低金價。
黃金之所以成為變現對象，並不代表其基本面突然轉差，而是因為市場流動性高，且經歷先前漲勢後，投資人仍累積可觀獲利。相較於難以脫手或已經大幅虧損的風險資產，出售黃金更容易迅速取得現金。
彭博專欄作家懷特（Simon White）指出，黃金過去就不是、現在也不是流動性避險工具。當投資人需要填補其他市場的損失時，黃金往往會成為優先變現的資產。高盛奎因今年3月也曾提醒，在市場爭相取得現金時，黃金未必是最安全的避風港。
高盛Delta One業務主管普里沃羅茨基（Rich Privorotsky）周五表示，長天期債券市場可能已開始反映政策失誤風險，當時殖利率下滑、損益兩平通膨率收窄，但股市與黃金卻同步遭到拋售。他認為，市場焦點正從通膨轉向經濟成長與流動性問題，AI相關部位原本的資金輪動，也已演變成全面性清算。
當被迫變現的賣壓跌破重要價格關卡，量化交易與趨勢策略又可能進一步放大跌勢。瑞銀指出，黃金期貨未平倉合約大幅減少，可能部分來自金價跌破技術關卡後觸發的系統性放空；趨勢追蹤策略（CTA）跟進賣出，加上市場傳出知名投資人卓肯米勒（Stanley Druckenmiller）放空白銀，進一步加劇市場跌勢。

期貨賣壓仍未出清 ETF持倉將面臨考驗

金價加速跌向每盎司3500美元之際，市場仍在觀察賣壓是否已經出清。
瑞銀全球研究策略師Joni Teves在11月20日報告中指出，這波跌勢發生前，市場原有部位相對精簡，因此即使金價大幅下跌，恐慌程度仍較過去一些市場修正時期溫和。
瑞銀認為，賣壓目前仍集中在期貨市場。自上周以來，黃金期貨未平倉合約已減少逾600萬盎司，部分可能是金價跌破技術關卡後，觸發系統性交易策略賣出所致。
期貨市場的潛在賣壓也可能尚未完全釋放。The Market Ear引述澳新銀行（ANZ）周中估算指出，芝商所（CME）的投機部位雖已清算近200噸黃金，但淨多頭部位仍達533噸，遠高於2022年及2023年約200噸的低點，意味後續仍可能有約200噸部位遭到清算。
相較之下，黃金ETF持倉至今仍展現韌性，但接下來幾天的資金流向將是重要觀察指標。瑞銀指出，黃金ETF持倉目前維持穩定，不過相關數據有公布時差，市場還需要時間確認投資人是否開始撤資。
上一季黃金ETF約有166噸資金流入，當時金價主要在每盎司4000至4500美元之間交易。經過這波回檔後，先前進場的部分投資人已面臨明顯帳面虧損，持有意願也將受到考驗。
另一方面，逢低承接的買盤目前仍不明顯。瑞銀表示，投資人注意力受到其他市場牽制，加上市場開始考慮聯準會聯邦公開市場委員會（FOMC）可能升息50個基點，進一步壓抑買進意願。
實物黃金買家與官方機構也暫時採取觀望態度。儘管中國農曆新年消費旺季將於2027年2月初到來，但金價下跌速度過快，實物買家傾向等待市場止穩。
瑞銀統計顯示，2026年第三季央行淨買進184.1噸黃金，其他官方機構隱含購金量則為137.1噸，但過往經驗顯示，官方買家通常會避開市場波動劇烈的時期。
金價波動也明顯升高。黃金1個月隱含波動率已從10月的20%以下，升至本周25%以上；實際波動率則從上月約18%升至接近22%。瑞銀預期，官方買家可能等到波動率回落後才重新進場。
大型非官方持有者的動向同樣受到關注。瑞銀引用公開財報指出，Tether截至2026年第三季底持有約143噸黃金，較前一季減少約2%。黃金今年約占其總資產10%，高於過去幾年的3%至4%。
若其他條件不變，金價回檔15%將使黃金占Tether總資產的比重隨之下降。市場關注Tether是否會增持黃金，以維持約10%的配置比例，或選擇接受比重降低，甚至已經減持，仍有待下一份財報揭曉。

期權指標出現極端訊號 反彈機會與築底仍須區分

黃金連續9個交易日下跌，累計跌幅達600美元。The Market Ear數據顯示，黃金相對強弱指數（RSI）已降至數十年來低點之一，衍生性商品市場也出現罕見的超賣訊號。
奎因指出，11月20日，黃金3個月標準化25 Delta賣權與買權偏度（put-call skew），以及隱含波動率，均出現4至5個標準差的極端變化。其中，3個月隱含波動率從10月底約19，快速升至約27.6；雖仍低於今年2月金價大漲時的34至35，但升幅相當罕見。
期權市場的另一項重要變化，是投資人對下跌風險的避險需求急遽升高。這波多頭行情大部分時間，市場偏好買進看漲期權；如今看跌期權相對於看漲期權的需求，已升至多年高點。
奎因統計，自2022年底以來，每當黃金看跌與看漲期權偏度大幅攀升，約有70%的機率會在接下來一周內出現均值回歸。不過，期權偏度回落不代表現貨金價已經築底。
從技術面來看，金價下一個主要支撐位在每盎司3400美元附近的下降通道下緣，較周五3588美元的現貨價格仍有約5%的下跌空間。只要引發追加保證金壓力的科技股與AI交易去槓桿尚未結束，黃金短期內仍可能受到資金抽離影響。
儘管短期賣壓沉重，主要投行對黃金中長期走勢的看法尚未轉空。高盛雖在兩周內兩度下調金價目標，仍預期在央行購金支撐下，金價將於2027年底升至每盎司4650美元，並在聯準會重新啟動降息後，於2028年底進一步升至5600美元。
瑞銀也認為，短期市場壓力並未改變黃金作為資產多元配置工具的長期價值，長期投資人已可開始尋找布局機會。
paras_en: Global financial markets have recently faced synchronized selling pressure, and gold has not been spared. As the AI‑trading boom cools and tech stocks undergo a sharp correction, leveraged investors are hit with margin‑call demands and begin selling gold to raise cash, turning the traditional safe‑haven asset into a preferred source of liquidity.

From November 17‑20, over four trading days, international gold prices plunged 9%, breaking below $3,600 per ounce for the first time since September 2025. JPMorgan’s early‑morning report on Friday the 20th showed spot gold at $3,588 per ounce, while silver fell even faster, sliding 15% over the week.

The sell‑off in precious metals coincided with the correction in U.S. tech equities. On November 20, after the Anthropic (ANT‑US) IPO dampened market sentiment, the Nasdaq‑100 index dropped as much as 4.9% intraday.

Both Goldman Sachs’ trading desk and UBS Global Research noted that recent selling pressure has been concentrated in the gold futures market, and a volatility‑driven options indicator tracked by Goldman has shown an exceptionally rare extreme swing.

Gold’s decline unfolded in two phases, with margin calls acting as a key catalyst. The first phase, from November 10‑17, was driven mainly by shifting rate expectations. A higher‑than‑expected U.S. CPI for October and a string of hawkish comments from Fed officials forced the market to reassess the interest‑rate outlook.

Goldman’s daily market monitor cited St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem, who warned at the time that the economy might need “multiple rate hikes” before spring. During that period the U.S. dollar index rose 1.2%, the 10‑year real rate climbed 11 basis points, and the December 2027 SOFR futures fell 7 basis points.

Because gold yields no interest, a stronger dollar and rising real rates dampened its appeal. The CFTC’s latest positioning report showed that during the 4.1% drop in gold from November 10‑17, speculative money was clearly exiting the market.

Goldman senior futures trader Robert Quinn estimated on November 21 that managed funds, other reportable positions and unreportable positions together sold about $9.3 billion of gold, offsetting the previous week’s buying. Roughly $5.8 billion of long positions were closed and about $3.5 billion of new short positions were added.
Net speculative long exposure in gold fell from a September peak of roughly $130 billion to about $72 billion, a new low not seen in about a year and a half.

However, the second‑phase drop from November 17‑20 cannot be explained solely by the dollar or rates. Quinn noted that gold fell 9% over those four days, the December‑to‑spot (EFP) spread weakened, and open‑interest in futures fell $7.3 billion, while the dollar’s rally clearly moderated and real rates even retreated. Most of the price loss, he said, moved in lockstep with the Nasdaq’s sharp fall.

This pattern suggests that margin‑call mechanisms are transmitting pressure across asset classes. When the AI‑trading surge receded and stocks slumped, leveraged investors had to raise cash to cover losses elsewhere, forcing them to liquidate gold holdings.

Goldman investment‑research analysts Lina Thomas and Daan Struyven warned in their 2027 precious‑metals outlook that the uncertainty of the AI‑investment cycle could trigger a similar scenario: a market crash that triggers margin calls would likely lead investors to sell gold first, pushing prices lower.

Gold’s role as a liquidation asset does not imply a sudden deterioration in fundamentals; rather, its high liquidity and the sizable unrealised gains accumulated after the prior rally make it an easy source of cash. Compared with illiquid or heavily‑loss‑making risk assets, selling gold provides a quick way to obtain funds.

Bloomberg columnist Simon White observed that gold has never been, and is not now, a pure liquidity‑safe‑haven tool. When investors need to cover losses in other markets, gold often becomes the first asset they cash out. Goldman’s Quinn also warned in March that, in a scramble for cash, gold may not be the safest harbor.

Goldman Delta‑One head Rich Privorotsky said on Friday that long‑dated bond markets may already be pricing in policy‑mistake risk, with yields slipping and breakeven‑inflation narrowing, yet both equities and gold were being sold off together. He believes market focus is shifting from inflation to growth and liquidity, and the capital that once rotated into AI‑related positions is now being cleared across the board.

When forced‑sale pressure breaches key price thresholds, quantitative and trend‑following strategies can amplify the decline. UBS noted that the sharp drop in open‑interest for gold futures may partly stem from systematic shorting triggered by the breach of technical levels; CTA trend‑following funds then added to the sell‑off, and rumors that famed investor Stanley Druckenmiller was shorting silver further intensified the market slide.
Futures‑selling pressure remains unresolved, putting ETF holdings to the test. As gold races toward $3,500 per ounce, the market is still watching to see whether the sell‑off has fully exhausted.

UBS Global Research strategist Joni Teves wrote on November 20 that, before this decline, market positions were relatively lean, so even a steep price drop is generating less panic than in past correction episodes.

UBS believes the remaining sell‑pressure is still concentrated in the futures market. Since last week, open‑interest in gold futures has shrunk by more than 6 million ounces, partly due to systematic trading rules kicking in after the price broke technical barriers.

Potential futures pressure may not be fully released yet. The Market Ear cited an ANZ mid‑week estimate that, although CME speculative positions have cleared roughly 200 tons of gold, net long exposure still stands at 533 tons – far above the ~200‑ton lows seen in 2022‑23 – implying another ~200 tons could still be liquidated.

By contrast, gold‑ETF holdings have remained resilient so far, but upcoming fund‑flow data will be a key gauge. UBS says ETF positions are currently stable, though reporting lags mean the market still needs time to confirm whether investors are beginning to pull out.

In the prior quarter, gold ETFs attracted about 166 tons of inflows when gold was trading between $4,000‑$4,500 per ounce. After the recent pull‑back, many of those investors now face noticeable paper losses, testing their willingness to stay invested.

On the demand side, low‑price buying remains muted. UBS notes that investors’ attention is tied up in other markets and that expectations of a possible 50‑basis‑point Fed rate hike at the next FOMC meeting are dampening buying enthusiasm.

Physical gold buyers and sovereign institutions are also sitting on the sidelines. Although the Chinese Lunar New Year shopping season will begin in early February 2027, the rapid price decline has prompted physical buyers to wait for the market to stabilise.

UBS data show central banks bought a net 184.1 tons of gold in Q3 2026, while other official entities accumulated an implied 137.1 tons. Historical patterns suggest official buyers usually avoid periods of extreme market turbulence.

Gold’s volatility has risen sharply. One‑month implied volatility has climbed from below 20% in October to over 25% this week, while realized volatility has moved from roughly 18% last month to near 22%. UBS expects official buyers to wait for volatility to recede before re‑entering.

The actions of large non‑official holders are also under scrutiny. UBS cited public filings showing Tether held about 143 tons of gold at the end of Q3 2026, down roughly 2% from the prior quarter. Gold now makes up about 10% of its total assets, up from 3‑4% in previous years.

If gold falls another 15% under current conditions, Tether’s gold share would shrink accordingly. The market is watching whether Tether will increase its holdings to keep the roughly 10% allocation, accept a lower weight, or perhaps already be reducing its exposure – a question that will be answered in the next earnings release.

Option indicators have flashed extreme signals, and any rebound must be distinguished from a true bottom. Gold has fallen for nine consecutive trading days, wiping about $600 off the price. The Market Ear data show the gold Relative Strength Index has dropped to one of its lowest levels in decades, while derivative markets are showing rare oversold readings.

Quinn highlighted that on November 20 the 3‑month standardized 25‑Delta put‑call skew and implied volatility both moved 4‑5 standard deviations from the norm. The 3‑month implied volatility jumped from roughly 19 at the end of October to about 27.6 – still below the 34‑35 levels seen during the gold surge in February 2024, but the rise is unusually steep.

Another notable shift in the options market is the surge in demand for downside protection. Throughout most of the prior up‑trend, market participants favored buying calls; now put demand relative to calls has risen to multi‑year highs.

Quinn’s analysis since the end of 2022 shows that whenever the put‑call skew for gold widens dramatically, there is roughly a 70% chance of a mean‑reversion move within the following week. However, a retreat in skew does not mean spot gold has found a floor.

Technically, the next major support lies near $3,400 per ounce at the lower edge of the descending channel, leaving about 5% more downside from Friday’s $3,588 spot price. As long as margin‑call pressure from tech stocks and AI‑trading deleveraging persists, gold could continue to feel the outflow impact in the short term.

Despite heavy short‑term selling, major banks have not turned bearish on gold’s medium‑to‑long‑term outlook. Goldman, after cutting its price target twice in two weeks, still expects central‑bank buying to lift gold to $4,650 per ounce by the end of 2027 and to $5,600 by the end of 2028 after the Fed resumes rate cuts.
UBS shares the view that short‑term market stress does not alter gold’s long‑term value as a diversification tool, and that long‑term investors can now start looking for positioning opportunities.

items.title: 正式擠身1兆美元俱樂部！南韓11月前20天出口額年增102%  晶片狂飆294%
items.title_en: Officially Joins the $1 Trillion Club! South Korea’s Export Value Up 102% in First 20 Days of November, Chip Boom 294%
paras: 根據南韓關稅廳週一(23日)公佈的數據，在全球AI熱潮持續拉動晶片需求的背景下，該國11月上旬出口持續走高，年度出口額首次突破1兆美元。經工作日調整後的11月前20天出口額年增95.2%，10月同期增幅為65.9%。未經工作日調整的年增率為101.5%，進口年增39.4%，貿易順差271億美元。本月前20天出口額774億美元，延續10月同期617億美元的強勁動能。
受AI基礎建設投資熱潮帶動，南韓半導體需求旺盛，今年經濟成長超乎預期。南韓產業部表示，該國成為繼美國、德國、中國之後，第四個年度出口突破1兆美元的經濟體。
半導體需求火熱，也促使市場接連調高南韓經濟成長預期。南韓國有智庫韓國開發研究院上週將2027年經濟成長率估值從2.2%大幅上調至3.9%，IMF則預估2027年南韓經濟將成長 3.3%。

市場預估，南韓央行(BOK)將在週四(26日)會議上更新經濟成長與通膨預期，同時發布最新六個月利率路徑展望。該行8月曾預測，今年南韓經濟將成長3.3%、2027年成長 2.9%，此後央行已釋放訊號，經濟成長率顯著高於先前預判。BOK週四(26日)會議為本年度最後一次貨幣政策會議，經濟學家普遍預期將升息1碼至3.25%。在 7 月、8 月連續升息後，BOK上月維持利率不變，意在觀察高借貸成本帶來的影響。
受惠於出口與投資大幅回暖，南韓今年Q3經濟成長率季增1%，超出市場預期，但私人消費意外收縮，這也說明晶片景氣紅利尚未廣泛傳導至居民端。
通膨黏性持續，進一步支持收緊貨幣政策的理由。南韓上月消費者物價指數(CPI)年增2.8%，核心通膨同樣維持2.8%，兩項指標均高於BOK的2%通膨目標。
paras_en: According to data released by South Korea’s Customs Service on Monday (the 23rd), export values continued to rise in the first half of November amid a global AI-driven surge in chip demand, pushing the country’s annual export total past the $1 trillion mark for the first time. Adjusted for weekdays, export value for the first 20 days of November was up 95.2% year‑on‑year, compared with a 65.9% increase for the same period in October. The unadjusted year‑on‑year growth rate was 101.5%, imports rose 39.4% year‑on‑year, and the trade surplus stood at $27.1 billion. Export value for the first 20 days of the month reached $77.4 billion, sustaining the strong momentum seen in October’s $61.7 billion.

Driven by a wave of AI infrastructure investment, demand for South Korean semiconductors has been robust, and this year’s economic growth has exceeded expectations. The Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy said the country has become the fourth economy—after the United States, Germany and China—to see annual exports break the $1 trillion threshold.

The hot semiconductor demand has also prompted the market to repeatedly raise South Korea’s growth outlook. The state‑run think‑tank Korea Development Institute last week sharply upgraded its 2027 growth forecast from 2.2% to 3.9%, while the IMF projects South Korean GDP to grow 3.3% in 2027.

Markets expect the Bank of Korea (BOK) to update its growth and inflation forecasts at its Thursday (the 26th) meeting and to release a new six‑month interest‑rate path outlook. In August the bank had projected 3.3% growth for this year and 2.9% for 2027; since then it has signaled that growth is likely to be markedly higher than earlier estimates. The Thursday meeting is the final monetary‑policy session of the year, and economists broadly anticipate a 0.25‑percentage‑point rate hike to 3.25%. After consecutive hikes in July and August, the BOK left rates unchanged last month to gauge the impact of higher borrowing costs.

Benefiting from a sharp rebound in both exports and investment, South Korea’s Q3 GDP grew 1% quarter‑on‑quarter, beating market expectations, although private consumption unexpectedly contracted, indicating that the chip‑sector boom has not yet fully filtered through to households.

Sticky inflation continues to underpin the case for tighter monetary policy. South Korea’s consumer price index (CPI) rose 2.8% year‑on‑year last month, with core inflation also at 2.8%, both above the BOK’s 2% inflation target.

items.title: 馬斯克示警AI產業明年恐現現金荒！資料中心延宕成導火線、企業還要籌數千億美元
items.title_en: Musk Warns AI Industry May Face Cash Crunch Next Year; Data‑Center Delays Sparked as Trigger, Companies May Need to Raise Hundreds of Billions
paras: 馬斯克示警，人工智慧（AI）產業明年恐面臨嚴重現金短缺，資料中心併網與投運延遲是關鍵原因。由於AI業者必須持續投入鉅額資金擴充算力，若基礎設施建設進度落後，企業可能還得額外籌措數千億美元資金，進一步加重融資壓力。
馬斯克周日（22日）在社群平台X回應一則貼文時表示，明年的現金短缺情況也將「非常嚴重」。他指出，資料中心投運延遲將迫使AI公司額外籌集「數千億美元」，並質疑這筆資金究竟要從何而來。
馬斯克回應的原始貼文提到，半導體製造商的股票估值相較於預期獲利偏低，可能反映投資人對晶片業者能否持續維持高速獲利成長抱持疑慮，也顯示短期內資料中心建設可能面臨阻礙。

算力擴張受制於資料中心進度

AI業者營收持續成長，但資本支出也同步攀升。Meta(META-US) 、微軟(MSFT-US) 及Anthropic(ANT-US) 等業者雖然營收增加，仍持續投入鉅額資金確保算力供應。
然而，資料中心建設近期面臨多重阻力，包括建設所在地社區反對、施工延誤，以及美國期中選舉民主黨取得勝利等因素。
缺乏穩定的資料中心網路，AI業者便難以擴大運算規模，滿足投資人對業務成長的期待；對資料中心營運商而言，數十億美元投資若因工程延宕而無法如期投入營運，也意味著收入進帳時間跟著推遲。
馬斯克指出，要讓如此龐大的算力順利接上電力、完成冷卻並維持穩定運作，難度高得驚人。
上周美股重挫，也讓AI泡沫疑慮從市場討論進一步反映在交易表現上。標普500指數與道瓊工業指數均進入修正區間，代表兩大指數較近期高點至少下跌10%，部分市場人士據此認為，AI泡沫可能已經破裂。
馬斯克的質疑凸顯AI產業面臨的資金矛盾：業者必須在營收完全實現前持續投入資本，而投資回收速度又取決於資料中心建設進度。一旦工程延誤，資金缺口便可能需要透過外部融資填補，規模甚至達數千億美元。
不過，在目前市場環境下，籌資難度也有所提高。科技股回檔壓低股權融資的估值基礎，而監管機構對放空交易的限制，也反映市場情緒趨於緊張。
paras_en: Musk warned that the artificial intelligence (AI) industry could face a severe cash shortage next year, with data‑center interconnection and delayed commissioning being the key reasons. Because AI firms must continuously pour massive funds into expanding compute capacity, a lag in infrastructure construction could force companies to raise an additional several hundred billion dollars, further intensifying financing pressure.

On Sunday (the 22nd), Musk replied to a post on the social platform X, saying the cash shortage next year will be "very serious." He noted that delays in data‑center commissioning will compel AI companies to raise "hundreds of billions of dollars" and questioned where that money would come from.

The original post Musk responded to mentioned that semiconductor manufacturers’ stock valuations appear low relative to expected earnings, possibly reflecting investors’ doubts about whether chip makers can sustain high profit growth and indicating that data‑center construction could face short‑term obstacles.

Compute expansion is constrained by data‑center progress. AI firms’ revenues keep growing, but capital expenditures rise in tandem. Companies such as Meta (META‑US), Microsoft (MSFT‑US) and Anthropic (ANT‑US) are increasing revenue yet continue to pour huge sums into securing compute supply.

However, recent data‑center construction faces multiple hurdles, including community opposition at build sites, construction delays, and factors such as the Democratic Party’s victory in the U.S. midterm elections.

Without a stable data‑center network, AI firms struggle to scale computing power to meet investors’ growth expectations; for data‑center operators, billions of dollars of investment delayed by construction setbacks means revenue streams are pushed back as well.
Musk pointed out that connecting such massive compute capacity to power, completing cooling, and maintaining stable operation is astonishingly difficult.

Last week’s sharp drop in U.S. equities also turned AI‑bubble concerns from market discussion into trading performance. Both the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average entered correction territory, meaning each index fell at least 10% from recent highs, leading some market participants to believe the AI bubble may have burst.

Musk’s doubts highlight the funding paradox facing the AI sector: firms must keep investing capital before revenues are fully realized, while the speed of return depends on data‑center construction. If projects are delayed, the funding gap may need to be filled by external financing, potentially reaching hundreds of billions of dollars.

However, in the current market environment, raising capital has become harder. The pullback in tech stocks depresses the valuation base for equity financing, and regulatory limits on short‑selling reflect increasingly tense market sentiment.

items.title: 美股恐更震盪！VIX飆近40創2025年4月來最高  選擇權交易員積極備戰
items.title_en: US Stocks May Experience More Volatility! VIX Soars Near 40, Highest Since April 2025, Options Traders Brace
paras: 美股連日急瀉，市場表面平靜被徹底撕開，那斯達克100指數上周四、五兩天暴跌約8%，標普500指數較高點回落逾10%，芝加哥期權交易所波動率指數(VIX)上周五(20日)飆升至2025年4月關稅風暴以來最高水位，選擇權市場正為接下來更頻繁、更劇烈的震盪做準備。
這波拋售由多重疑慮疊加觸發：美債殖利率攀升、民主黨在期中選舉全面勝出可能收緊AI監管，加上Anthropic備受矚目的IPO才過一天，市場對AI交易能否延續的信心迅速降溫。衍生商品策略師直言，市場「脆弱性」正明顯升高，長時間低波動的平靜，愈來愈容易被突發式震盪打斷。
美銀全球股票衍生品主管Ben Bowler指出，過去一年指數波動率之所以被壓住，關鍵在個股相關性處於數十年低點，個別股票大幅波動彼此抵銷，市場選擇板塊輪動而非全面崩裂，加上0DTE(當日到日期權)賣盤擴張、投資者對AI經濟潛力的亢奮，共同撐住了表面平靜。
但這層緩衝正在失效。VIX波動幅度已回到去年4月關稅震盪時期水準，個股相關性升至3月以來最高，0DTE資金流向開始反轉，意味著「個別風險」有機會升級為「指數風險」。
Bowler預警，2026年個股脆弱性事件仍普遍，科技股今年此類事件數量恐將創下30多年來第二高，僅次於2025年。
換言之，一旦出現廣泛衝擊把個股相關性推得更高，指數波動率將被動放大，這正是選擇權交易員眼下最防範的情境。防跌成本已經開始變貴，市場從「輪動」走向「共振」的距離，比想像中更近。
paras_en: US stocks have been falling for several days, and the market’s calm façade has been torn apart. The Nasdaq 100 fell about 8% over Thursday and Friday last week, the S&P 500 dropped more than 10% from its peak, and the Chicago Board Options Exchange volatility index (VIX) surged to its highest level since the April 2025 tariff storm on Friday (the 20th), as the options market prepares for more frequent and severe swings.

This selloff was triggered by a combination of concerns: rising U.S. Treasury yields, the possibility that the Democratic Party’s sweeping midterm election win could tighten AI regulation, and the fact that Anthropic’s highly anticipated IPO was only a day old, causing confidence in the continuation of AI trading to cool rapidly. Derivatives strategists have said the market’s “fragility” is clearly increasing, and the long period of low volatility calm is becoming more susceptible to sudden shocks.

Ben Bowler, head of global equity derivatives at Bank of America, noted that the reason index volatility was suppressed over the past year was that individual stock correlations were at a multi‑decade low, with large swings in individual stocks offsetting each other. The market rotated through options sectors rather than collapsing wholesale, and the expansion of 0‑DTE (same‑day expiration) selling, coupled with investor enthusiasm for AI’s economic potential, helped maintain the surface calm.

But that buffer is breaking down. VIX volatility has returned to the level seen during the tariff shock in April last year, individual stock correlations have risen to the highest level since March, and 0‑DTE capital flows are reversing, meaning that “individual risk” could upgrade to “index risk.”

Bowler warns that individual stock fragility events will remain common in 2026, and that the number of such events for tech stocks this year could be the second highest in more than 30 years, only behind 2025.

In other words, once a widespread shock pushes individual stock correlations higher, index volatility will be passively amplified, which is the scenario options traders are most concerned about right now.
